q: Halogens (F2, Cl2, Br2, I2) are diatomic molecules. More reactive ____ is the most reactive.
e: Fluorine is the most electronegative and reactive of all elements.

q: Fluorine and chlorine are gases, bromine is a ____ and iodine is a solid at room temperature.
e: Bromine is the only liquid halogen at room temperature.

q: Halogens are highly electronegative elements. Since the essential electronic structure of halogen is ns2 np5, they are very ____ .
e: High reactivity is due to their tendency to gain electrons.

q: None of the halogens can be found in nature in their elemental forms. They are found as salts of the ____ .
e: Halides are compounds formed from halogens and metals.

q: In the laboratory, halogen is prepared by heating sodium or potassium halide with manganese(IV) oxide and concentrated ____ acid.
e: Concentrated sulphuric acid is used to produce halogens.

q: Chlorine is prepared from the mixture of sodium chloride, manganese(IV) oxide and concentrated sulphuric acid on heating. It is collected by the upward displacement of ____ .
e: Chlorine is less soluble in water and heavier than air.

q: Fluorine is a very pale yellow gas. It is the lightest halogen and exists as a highly ____ gas.
e: Fluorine's toxicity makes it dangerous to handle.

q: Chlorine is a pale green gas with a choking, unpleasant smell. Chlorine is very poisonous if inhaled even in ____ quantities.
e: Even small amounts of chlorine can be harmful.

q: Bromine is a heavy, reddish brown, volatile liquid. It has a choking, irritating smell. Liquid bromine causes ____ on the flesh.
e: Bromine can cause severe skin irritation and burns.

q: Iodine is a purple-black shiny solid with an irritating smell. Iodine sublimes rapidly when heated, forming a violet ____ .
e: Sublimation is the transition from solid to gas without passing through a liquid phase.

q: Halogens react with most compounds containing ____ .
e: Halogens readily react with hydrogen to form hydrogen halides.

q: When a tube containing equal volumes of chlorine and hydrogen is exposed to sunlight, it ____ .
e: This reaction is highly exothermic and produces hydrogen chloride.

q: Chlorine reacts vigorously with metals to form metal ____ .
e: Metal chlorides are formed through direct reactions with metals.

q: Iron + chlorine -> ____ .
e: Iron(II) chloride is formed when iron reacts with chlorine.

q: Copper + chlorine -> ____ .
e: Copper(II) chloride is produced from the reaction of copper with chlorine.

q: Bromine combines readily with most metals to form ____ .
e: Bromides are the products of reactions between bromine and metals.

q: Phosphorus burns spontaneously in chlorine to form ____ .
e: Phosphorus(III) chloride is formed from the reaction of phosphorus with chlorine.

q: Chlorine reacts with water to form hypochlorous acid and ____ acid.
e: This reaction produces two acids from chlorine and water.

q: The HOCI slowly decomposes to nascent ____ .
e: Nascent oxygen is highly reactive and can bleach substances.

q: Chlorine will bleach moist litmus papers. This is used as a test for ____ .
e: Bleaching indicates the presence of chlorine gas.

q: Halides are formed when halogens combine with ____ .
e: Halides are ionic compounds formed from halogens and metals.

q: The presence of chloride, bromide or iodide ions can be tested by adding ____ nitrate solution.
e: Silver nitrate is used to detect halide ions by forming precipitates.
